description: Critical endgame positions from AI Chessathon rounds 40 and 41.

positions.label: Team Keble, White move 39
positions.diagnosis: V5 chose h4 with a winning position; Stockfish preferred activating the passed d-pawn with d5.

positions.label: Team Keble, White move 40
positions.diagnosis: V5 spent about 1.4 seconds on Qa7+, losing much of a winning advantage; Qd5 centralises with checks and supports the passer.

positions.label: Team Keble, White move 41
positions.diagnosis: V5 grabbed a pawn with Qxg7 instead of maintaining queen activity and the winning attack with Qa8.

positions.label: Team Keble, White move 42
positions.diagnosis: V5 took another pawn with Qxh6 instead of using g5 to restrict the king and preserve the attack.

positions.label: Team Keble, White move 43
positions.diagnosis: V5 allowed ...c2 with Qf4 and the evaluation fell from winning to equal; Qg7 retains control and checks.

positions.label: this team, Black move 26
positions.diagnosis: V5 chose Re6 and moved from roughly equal to clearly worse; Nc8 keeps the rook active and contains White's pieces.

positions.label: this team, Black move 38
positions.diagnosis: V5 chose passive Rd7 instead of Rb5 and turned a defensible ending into a substantially worse one.

positions.label: this team, Black move 41
positions.diagnosis: V5 grabbed the g2 pawn with Nxg2 instead of eliminating the active bishop with Nxf5.

positions.label: this team, Black move 47
positions.diagnosis: V5 missed Kh7 in a rook-and-bishop ending and gave away a substantial part of its drawing chances.

positions.label: this team, Black move 51
positions.diagnosis: V5 played Rc7 instead of the active defensive move Rf6 and missed another near-equal defensive chance.

positions.label: this team, Black move 52
positions.diagnosis: V5 chose Kf7 rather than activating the rook with Rf7 and lost the final practical drawing opportunity.
